'''Hermi Odle''' was a [[Gender|male]] [[Baragwin]] [[gangster]] who worked as a weapons specialist and as the personal [[armorer]] of the [[Hutt]] [[crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure]], helping to craft defenses for the Hutt's [[Boba Fett's Palace|palace]] on the [[planet]] [[Tatooine]]. He was part of a crowd that refused to back Jabba's [[majordomo]], [[Bib Fortuna]], when [[Boba Fett]] confronted Fortuna at the palace while looking for Jabba.

In [[4 ABY]], Odle was present in Jabba's [[throne]] room when the [[droid]]s [[R2-D2]] and [[C-3PO]] delivered a message to Jabba from the [[Jedi Knight]] [[Luke Skywalker]], and laughed when the Hutt declared he would not be bargaining with the [[Jedi]] for the freedom of the [[smuggler]] [[Han Solo]]. He was later present when Skywalker arrived at the palace and [[Death|killed]] Jabba's pet [[rancor]] [[Pateesa]].

==Biography==
===Shady thug===
{{Quote|You know who I am. ''Boba Fett''. You know what that means. All of you want to live. Who doesn't? But I promise. Fight me… some of you die. Maybe ''most'' of you. And you'd be dying… for ''him''. Doesn't seem fair, does it?|Boba Fett speaks to the crowd that Odle is part of|<ref name="WotBH 1">[[War of the Bounty Hunters 1|''War of the Bounty Hunters'' 1]]</ref>}}
Hermi Odle was a [[Baragwin]] [[Gender|male]]<ref name="Force Collection" /> [[gangster]]<ref name="Geektionary">''[[Star Wars: Geektionary: The Galaxy from A - Z]]''</ref> with a shady past<ref name="Hermi Odle" /> who was on the payroll of the [[crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure]]<ref name="Geektionary" /> as the [[Hutt]]'s personal [[armorer]].<ref name="CVD">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition]]''</ref> He also worked as a weapons specialist and helped to craft the defences of [[Boba Fett's Palace|Jabba's Palace]]<ref name="Force Collection" /> on the [[desert]] [[planet]] [[Tatooine]], where he could often be found.<ref name="Geektionary" />

[[File:BobaVsFortuna3-WOTBH1.png|thumb|right|300px|Odle was among a crowd that refused to defend Bib Fortuna.]]
Shortly after the [[smuggler]] [[Han Solo]] was frozen in [[carbonite]]<ref name="SW2">[[Star Wars (2020) 2|''Star Wars'' (2020) 2]]</ref> in [[3 ABY]],<ref name="Galactic Atlas" /> Odle walked past the [[bounty hunter]] [[Amanaman]] and Solo's ally [[Landonis Balthazar Calrissian|Lando Calrissian]] as Calrissian asked Amanaman to keep an [[eye]] out for the bounty hunter [[Boba Fett]] for him.<ref name="SW2" /> Jabba later put a [[bounty]] on Fett after the bounty hunter had Solo's frozen form stolen from him while trying to deliver it to Jabba. Fett then traveled to Jabba's Palace to confront the Hutt, but was greeted at the gate by the Hutt's [[majordomo]], [[Bib Fortuna]].<ref name="WotBH 1" />

Fortuna explained that Jabba was unavailable as he was attending an [[Auction for Han Solo|auction]] for Solo being held by [[Crimson Dawn]]. A crowd including Odle then emerged behind Fortuna, some with their weapons aimed at Fett, as the majordomo suggested that the hunter leave. Fett instead spoke to the crowd, asking if it was worth potentially dying for Fortuna's sake. The crowd lowered their weapons, and Fett passed by Odle as he walked into the palace with Fortuna to see the auction invitation.<ref name="WotBH 1" />

===Rescue of Han Solo===
[[File:LaughingHermi-ROTJ.png|thumb|left|300px|Hermi Odle worked in Jabba's Palace.]]
In [[4 ABY]],<ref name="Date">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates the events of {{Film|VI}} to [[4 ABY]].</ref> he was present in the palace when the [[droid]]s [[R2-D2]] and [[C-3PO]] arrived<ref name="ROTJ" /> early one [[Standard day|morning]]<ref name="Darkside">''[[Return of the Jedi: Beware the Power of the Dark Side!]]''</ref> with a [[Hologram|holographic]] message from their master, the [[Jedi Knight]] [[Luke Skywalker]]. In the message, Skywalker asked to bargain with Jabba for the freedom of [[Han Solo]], a [[Prisoner|imprisoned]] [[smuggler]] that the Hutt held frozen in [[carbonite]] and displayed on his [[throne]] room wall, and gifted him the two droids as a sign of good will. After the recording finished, Jabba announced that he had no interest in giving up his favorite decoration, causing Odle, who was stood in front of Solo's frozen form, to laugh.<ref name="ROTJ" />

[[File:HermiOdleShasaTiel-RotJAVA.png|thumb|right|250px|Hermi Odle was a bizarre looking Baragwin, but was more dangerous than his appearance suggested.]]
Odle was later [[sleep]]ing in one of the throne room's booths<ref name="ROTJ" /> the morning after a night of celebrations at the palace following<ref name="Darkside" /> the capture of [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] after she had freed Solo from carbonite. As the Baragwin dozed alongside Jabba and many other court members, Skywalker arrived at the palace and used [[mind trick]]s to reach the throne room, where the Hutt's [[majordomo]], [[Bib Fortuna]], woke the crime lord up. As the court also rose, Skywalker demanded that Solo, Organa, and the [[Wookiee]] [[Chewbacca]] be released, threatening Jabba with a [[DL-18 blaster pistol|blaster pistol]] when he refused.<ref name="ROTJ" />

Jabba then dropped Skywalker, and the unfortunate [[Gamorrean]] guard [[Jubnuk]], through a trap door into a pit below the throne room. The court watched as Jabba's pet [[rancor]], [[Pateesa]], devored Jubnuk before being [[Death|killed]] by Skywalker, outraging Jabba. Odle remained in the booth, by this point standing, as Skywalker, Solo, and Chewbacca were dragged before the Hutt and sentenced to death. Jabba and much of his court then traveled to the [[Great Pit of Carkoon]] to witness the executions, but the captives managed to turn the tables on their captors and killed the crime lord and many of his followers.<ref name="ROTJ" />

==Personality and traits==
Hermi Odle was a massive Baragwin<ref name="Geektionary" /> who stood 2.1 [[meter]]s.<ref name="Hermi Odle" /> A bizarre creature,<ref name="CVD" /> his head and [[Mouth|lips]] fell to the level of his throat, which gave the impression that the gangster was a hunchback.<ref name="Geektionary" /> However, wise members of Jabba's court knew that he was far more dangerous than his stopped posture, shuffling gait, and drooping lip suggested.<ref name="Hermi Odle" /> He had [[Color|yellow]] [[eye]]s and mottled pink and purple skin.<ref name="ROTJ" />

==Equipment==
Odle wore a tattered [[Cape|cloak]] and [[clothing]]<ref name="Geektionary" /> which were all brown in color.<ref name="ROTJ" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:HermiOdle-VE.png|thumb|right|250px|The Hermi Odle costume measured 201 centimeters, by 308 centimeters, by 102 centimeters]]
In the current ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], Hermi Odle first appeared in the [[original trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']],<ref name="ROTJ" /> which was released on [[May 25]], [[1983]].<ref name="YBY">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, New Edition]]''</ref> He was played by the mime artist [[Phil Herbert]],<ref name="Actor">{{WebCite|url=https://www.scifinow.co.uk/news/return-of-the-jedi-star-signs-up-for-norwich-sci-fi-convention|text=Return of the Jedi Star Signs Up For Norwich Sci-Fi Convention|author=Hoare, James|date=29-06-2012|archivedate=20210118010739}}</ref> who was credited as a mime artist on the film.<ref name="ROTJ" /> The full costume was based on a maquette of the character and measured 201 centimeters tall, 308 centimeters in diameter, and 102 centimeters wide<ref name="Chronicles">''[[Star Wars Chronicles]]''</ref> and was designed by [[Phil Tippett]]. Creature builder [[Kirk Thatcher]] thinks it may have been [[Tony McVey]] who built the outfit, likely in a single afternoon.<ref name="Archeology">{{YouTube|video=RWw8-s_a0vM|text=Star Wars: Return of the Jedi - Cantina Archeology Part 3: Behind The Scenes of Jabba's Palace|channel=@CredibleNerds|name=The Credible Nerds}}</ref> The palace throne room scenes filmed between [[January 25]] and [[February 8]], [[1982]] on Stage 8 at [[Elstree Studios]].<ref name="MakingOf">''[[The Making of Return of the Jedi]]''</ref>

The character was listed as number 26 on list of creatures being made for the film from [[November 4]], [[1981]], which gave Hermi Odle as its production name, but also had "Hemmy Moroid" as a nickname."<ref name="Creature History">{{SW|url=news/return-of-the-jedi-creature-history-with-pablo-hidalgo|text=''Return of the Jedi'' Creature History with Pablo Hidalgo|nolive=1}}</ref> Odle's name is likely a take on 'Hear Me Yodel'.<ref name="Databank">{{DB|character|hermiodle|Odle, Hermi}}</ref> In the film's second draft, Odle sat on C-3PO while Jabba's pet [[Salacious B. Crumb]] tormented the droid during the barge scene. R2-D2 then saved C-3PO by giving Crumb and then Odle electric shocks to force them off the droid.<ref name="BTM">{{InsiderCite|58|Behind the Magic}}</ref> This scene was used in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] [[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|novelization]] of the film by [[James Kahn]],<ref name="Novelization">[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi'' novelization]]</ref> which was released prior to the film on [[May 12]], 1983,<ref name="YBY" /> therefore marking the character's first appearance in the Legends continuity.<ref name="Novelization" /> The name was first used [[in-universe]] in the current canon by the [[Star Wars video games|mobile card game]] ''[[Star Wars: Force Collection]]'',<ref name="Force Collection" /> which initially launched in [[2013]]. Although the launch of ''Force Collection'' predates<ref name="Force Collection release">{{SW|url=news/announcing-star-wars-force-collection|text=Announcing Star Wars: Force Collection|nolive=1}}</ref> the ''Star Wars'' canon reset of [[2014]],<ref name="Legends">{{SW|url=news/the-legendary-star-wars-expanded-universe-turns-a-new-page|text=The Legendary Star Wars Expanded Universe Turns a New Page}}</ref> [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] member [[Leland Chee]] confirmed that the game was kept updated to fit with canon.<ref name="Twitter">{{Twitter|holocronkeeper|status/846807700482666496|[[Leland Chee]]|quote=I'm not gonna go through the trouble of changing them and I don't have any reason to believe currently that anyone would. […] On the off-chance that we DID have a current need to change any of these, we would have for Force Collection.|archivedate=20210505080831}} — [[Leland Chee]] of the [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] has confirmed that [[in-universe]] information from ''[[Star Wars: Force Collection]]'' conforms with ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]].</ref>
